correctness.rationale: A scalar Bass-with-attrition equation is a Riccati flow with strictly positive fractional-linear matrix lift. Both projective composition denominators are positive on the invariant adopter interval, so the order difference has a quadratic numerator. The exact same-churn matrices A and B produce cross-numerator 128(3697x^2-3962x+493), with strict alternating signs at initial shares 0, 1/2, and 1, hence exactly two interior simple reversals. Perturbations preserve them. A common equilibrium fixes both flow maps and makes their composed derivatives agree, forcing a double polynomial root and no reversal. Standard-library checker verifies exact algebra plus 200 independent numerical flow comparisons.

value.rationale: Two fixed marketing campaigns may change their preferred order twice as the current adopted fraction varies, contradicting a natural one-crossover intuition even under identical customer departure rates. The analytical ceiling proves sharp maximality, a strict parameter neighborhood demonstrates robustness, and the shared-equilibrium obstruction explains why the classic attrition-free Bass model cannot realize the effect. This answers a concrete structural decision-model question, without claiming empirical occurrence or broad optimization.
